title: Romeo and Juliet, Shakespeare
subtitle: c. 1595
subject: litterature
description: Around 1595, two lovers in Verona die in less than five days. Shakespeare compresses a romance into a social tragedy: clan hatred destroys the young.

hero.hook: Five days from love at first sight to the grave: the most famous love tragedy in the world.

blocks.text: Around **1595**, **William Shakespeare** wrote **[[Romeo and Juliet]]**. We know it as the greatest love story of the stage. It is also a savage attack on inherited hatred between rival families. The two lovers do not die of bad luck alone: they pay for a city unable to protect its young from the violence of its clans.

blocks.caption: The balcony scene: absolute love against the clans of Verona

sections.title: Shakespeare's alchemy: from novella to drama

blocks.text: Shakespeare did not invent the story. He drew above all on **Matteo Bandello**, a 16th-century Italian storyteller who was himself reworking older tales. His genius lies in **compression**: where his sources spread the action over months, Shakespeare squeezes it into **five days**. Every minute counts, and the disaster becomes unavoidable.
In Bandello, Juliet wakes before Romeo dies. Shakespeare cut that farewell to make the ending crueler.

The play opens almost like a comedy, full of wordplay and lively street scenes. Then **Mercutio**, a brilliant wit whose humor runs on **[[Cynicism]]**, dies halfway through the story. Lightness dies with him, and the tone tips into tragedy for good. Romeo had first played the part of **[[Medieval courtly love]]**, sighing over Rosaline before he discovered something far deeper and far more dangerous.

sections.title: A tragic machine: between chance and necessity

blocks.text: **Romeo Montague** and **Juliet Capulet** fall in love at a masked ball, neither knowing at first who the other is. The balcony scene celebrates love, but it also rejects the family name: “Deny thy father and refuse thy name.” The secret marriage performed by **Friar Laurence** was meant to calm the **[[vendetta]]** between the two houses.

blocks.caption: Romeo and Juliet: teenage passion caught in clan violence

blocks.text: Within hours **Tybalt** kills Mercutio, Romeo kills Tybalt in revenge, and Romeo is banished from Verona. An outbreak of **plague** delays the messenger who was to tell him that Juliet is not dead, only asleep from a potion. This is not divine fate alone: it is a chain of small accidents landing on a society already poisoned. The two suicides claim an absolute freedom in a world that leaves the lovers no room at all.
Romeo, doff thy name, and for that name, which is no part of thee, take all myself.

sections.title: Social responsibility and the sacrifice of the young

blocks.text: The play treats the feud as an engine of destruction. Montague and Capulet hate each other without even remembering why. The prologue speaks of an “ancient grudge” that breaks out into “new mutiny.” Juliet, barely **13**, is told to marry Count **Paris**. Romeo drifts in a melancholy his friends cannot understand.

The **Prince of Verona** stands for a law too weak to face the private militias of the two families. At the end, standing over the bodies of the young, he blames the parents: “All are punished.” The lovers are victims of a system that puts clan honor above personal happiness. Dante had already named the **Montecchi** and the **Cappelletti** in the 14th century, two hundred years before Shakespeare.

sections.title: A universal afterlife: from lyric poetry to modern gangs

blocks.text: The influence of the play is enormous. Shakespeare mixes religious devotion with physical passion and invents a new language of love for the English stage. His **[[Peripateticism]]**, the art of building thought through action and movement, is still taught as a dramatic model in drama schools around the world.

In the 20th century, **[[West Side Story]]** moved the conflict to New York: the **Sharks** and the **Jets** replaced the clans of Verona. The pattern still holds, since love for an outsider runs into the hatred of the group. Religious, racial, and social conflicts keep reusing Shakespeare's template.

**Romeo and Juliet** packs a teenage love story and an indictment of inherited violence into five days. Shakespeare shows that absolute love cannot survive in a society that prefers its old grudges to its living children.
